h.strategy: Use the retrieved work from other fields as a source of mechanisms that transfer to this system: redundancy and robustness in networks, complementarity versus substitution of inputs, bottlenecks and rate limits in flows, diminishing returns, and interference between processes. For each hypothesis, state which borrowed mechanism it instantiates, and use every mechanism at most twice. Do not condition on the current value of the edited field itself, and do not use conditions that simply make the edited part unused or disconnected; experts see both as obvious. Prefer interactions between two different fields where the predicted direction contradicts the naive expectation. Spread hypotheses across many edit fields and condition fields and both directions. In each 'why', give the mechanism and the specific comparison that would refute it.

hyps.why: A strong direct conv path tolerates a degraded branch, so the pooling penalty on edge 4 is smaller.
A skip on edge 4 gives an unsmoothed alternative to the pooled 2->3 path.
When a conv path carries the learned signal, a pooled direct bypass costs less.
Skips on both serial hops leave the 0->1->2 branch with no learned transformation.
With a skip on edge 4, the edge-0 conv is the only learned transformation on that path.
A skip on 2->3 forwards node-2 features unchanged, so edge-1 quality limits learned content.
A skip on the direct edge already provides a shortcut, so an extra skip on 1->2 is redundant.
A skip on the direct edge lets the output bypass the chain via node 1, so improving edge 0 matters less.
Node 2 already gets strong upstream input via edge 2, so a 1x1 on edge 1 adds little.
Stacked pooling on the serial path 0->1->3 compounds smoothing and loses detail.
